newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WHEATON TAKES ANOTHER STEP FORWARD TO REACH SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WHEATON TAKES ANOTHER STEP FORWARD TO REACH SEMIFINALS.

text.p: David Wheaton's return from
an eight-month layoff and foot surgery took another leap
forward Friday when he defeated Vince Spadea 6-3 4-6 6-2 to
reach the semifinals of the Legg Mason Tennis Classic.
Forced to qualify for the 56-man field after his once
lofty world ranking of number 12 dropped as low as 275,
Wheaton made Spadea the third successive seeded player he has
beaten. Earlier, he defeated Jason Stoltenberg (5) and Marzio
Martelli (12).
"I had surgery on my right heel at the end of March, so
I'm happy just to be able to play matches, much less win
them," said Wheaton, a one-time Wimbledon semifinalist.
"I feel I'm almost back to the form I had at last year's
U.S. Open."
Wheaton lost to Andre Agassi in the fourth round of the
Open at Flushing Meadows. Shortly thereafter, the troublesome
heal began to act up and he rested it.
"I was hoping that would do it, but it didn't," he said.
"Boy, am I glad I had the surgery done."
Wheaton made his first start on grass at Newport earlier
this month and reached the quarter-finals before losing to
Grant Stafford. He will play Petr Korda Saturday in his first
semifinal since Newport two years ago.
Second-seeded Korda advanced to the semifinals by slipping
by Germany's Tommy Haas 6-7 (2-7) 6-4 6-4 despite becoming ill
in the middle of the third set with the score tied at 3-3.
In the other semifinal, top seed Michael Chang will take
on New Zealander Brett Steven.
Chang defeated seventh-seeded Scott Draper 6-2 6-3, while
the 11th-seeded Steven beat unseeded Ranier Schuttler 6-3 6-3.
"I struggled a lot and my game was up and down through
most of the match," said Wheaton. "But that ended up helping
me as he (Spadea) probably couldn't get a read on me. It
wasn't super-hot out there and I'm thankful some clouds came
over in the third set."
